resources.string: Well done. Press A to go on.

This console has no touchscreen. Everything works with the buttons, and this short tutorial lets you try each of them. It takes about three minutes.\n\nPress A to go on and B to go back. Press Select to skip a step you already know.

A confirms: it opens what's selected and presses buttons on screen.

B goes back, one screen at a time.

X and Y do different things in each app and game.

Press each of them once.
The D-pad moves the selection around the screen: through lists, menus and buttons. The left stick does the same in menus.\n\nPress each direction once.
Games use both sticks. You can also press each stick in, like a button: that\'s L3 and R3.\n\nMove both sticks and watch the dots follow them, then press one stick in.
Press a stick in (L3 or R3)
L1 and R1 are the upper shoulder buttons, L2 and R2 the lower ones. Many apps use L1 and R1 to switch tabs or pages.\n\nPress each of them once.

Press FN on its own to get to the home screen from anywhere, even from a game. The home screen is Daijishou, where your games and apps are.\n\nTry it now: press FN. This tutorial comes back by itself a few seconds later.
Welcome back. That\'s all there is to it.

FN has a second job: hold it and press another button for a shortcut.\n\nHold FN and press Vol+ to make the screen brighter. Hold FN and press Vol− to make it darker. The volume buttons alone still change the volume.
Already at the brightest? Start with darker.
That was FN on its own, so the home screen opened. Hold FN down, then press the second button while you keep holding FN.
Hold FN and press Y to open your notifications and the Quick Settings, with tiles for things like Wi-Fi and Bluetooth.\n\nOpen it now, then close it again with FN + Y.

A few apps expect a touchscreen. For those, the right stick can move a mouse pointer. A clicks, L1 is a right click, and the left stick scrolls.\n\nTo turn it on or off, hold both sticks pressed in (L3 + R3) for a second.

A few apps expect a touchscreen. For those, the right stick can move a mouse pointer. A clicks, L1 is a right click, and the left stick scrolls.\n\nTo turn it on or off, hold both sticks pressed in (L3 + R3) for a second, or press FN + X.
Tap Power to put the console to sleep, and tap it again to wake it up.\n\nHold Power for a second to open the power menu: power off, restart and more. Press B to close the menu.
Tap Power to sleep, then again to wake up
Hold Power to open the menu, then B to close it

Put the SD card in a computer. Besides a small BOOT drive it shows a big drive called EASYROMS: that's for your games.

Give each system its own folder, named like nes, snes, gba, megadrive or psx.

Then open Daijishou (press FN), add a platform and pick its folder on EASYROMS. Daijishou lists the games and starts them in RetroArch or PPSSPP.
EASYROMS on this card: %1$s free of %2$s.

That\'s the basics.\n\nThe quick start guide explains more: emulators, speed and battery, going online, and what to do if something goes wrong. Open it here, from the Help icon in your app list, or from Settings > Quick start guide.

That\'s the basics. Forgot a shortcut? Hold FN on its own for a moment, in any app or game, to see them all.\n\nThe quick start guide explains more: emulators, speed and battery, going online, and what to do if something goes wrong. Open it here, from the Help icon in your app list, or from Settings > Quick start guide.
